page: Amazon Web Services r5d.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

A key feature of the r5d.4xlarge is its bundled local storage, consisting of a 600 GB NVMe SSD instance store. This local storage provides high-speed, low-latency read and write capabilities directly attached to the hypervisor. Networking is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% for tests like stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth scale to average levels in the middle 50% tier. Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput also perform in the average tier, reflecting stable multi-threaded capabilities.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5d.4xlarge balances high memory capacity with high-speed local NVMe storage, making it a viable option for workloads requiring fast scratch space without the overhead of network-attached storage. This hardware profile is appropriate for memory-intensive applications, database operations, caching layers like Redis, and moderate multi-threaded data processing tasks.
